assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin biology moved from gut-hormone physiology to some of the most consequential metabolic drugs in decades, with large effects on diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The discovery chain is clear and the lasting impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor agonist concept) and Knudsen (design of long-acting analogues liraglutide/semaglutide) span physiology to therapy. Mojsov's and others' contributions to identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide are credited and contested, and the three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple large outcome trials and global clinical adoption; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Knudsen and Mojsov (and others not on the list) is unresolved.
Whether the committee prefers basic physiology or the drug-development leg.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that blockade gives clinical benefit established the rationale for biologic therapy in rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease, psoriasis and other immune-mediated diseases. Conceptually clear and transformative for patient care.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the mechanistic work and first clinical trials with anti-TNF antibody, a compact and well-recognised pairing. Others (e.g. antibody developers such as Vilcek, Cerami and Tracey, and the TNF cloning groups) have claims that may be raised, but I have not verified the details.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of use with robust confirmation, Lasker award and the biologics class is mature; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether TNF biology and antibody engineering contributors deserve inclusion.
Prior prize history for related immunology could reduce urgency (uncertain).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, creating a new therapeutic modality with approved products and an expanding scope into autoimmunity. The conceptual and clinical impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) are plausible. Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner and others contributed foundational CAR concepts and may be omitted unfairly.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and long follow-up exist; toxicity, solid-tumour limitations and access remain, but the core discovery is robust and mature.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept (not on the credited list) is unresolved.
Long-term durability and safety are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic identification of SMN2 exon 7 splicing as targetable by antisense oligonucleotides led to nusinersen, which changed spinal muscular atrophy from a lethal infant disease into a treatable one. A clean path from molecular mechanism to a transformative therapy and a proof of principle for RNA-targeted medicine.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ASO target; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development at Ionis. The two-person pairing is coherent, though the discovery of the ISS-N1 target site by another group (Singh and colleagues, as I recall, unverified) may be raised.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong controlled trial data and long-term outcomes; mature enough, though the area is relatively recent.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the ISS-N1 target site.
Committee may regard it as therapeutic development more than fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA triggers type I interferon and inflammation, with deep relevance to infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus), cancer immunotherapy and ageing. Originality is high and the pathway is now textbook.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING; Ishikawa co-identified STING. Wu and Sun were co-authors in Chen's work. Two to three leaders are defensible, but the split between Chen and the STING discoverers is a real question.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across fields, yet clinical translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered an approved drug, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Barber, Ishikawa and the Chen group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Human genetics identified PCSK9 as a regulator of LDL receptor and LDL cholesterol; gain- and loss-of-function variants validated the target, leading to PCSK9 antibodies and siRNA drugs with proven cardiovascular benefit. A model of human genetics driving therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel and Boileau first reported gain-of-function mutations in familial hypercholesterolaemia; Seidah identified the proprotein convertase; Hobbs and Cohen showed loss-of-function variants lower LDL and coronary risk. Five credited people with real claims makes the three-person limit difficult and potentially unfair.
assessment.maturity: Excellent independent confirmation, outcome trials and approved drugs; timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among five contributors, especially the original Abifadel/Boileau discovery.
Statin precedent may reduce perceived novelty of the therapeutic concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and its successors turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a chronic manageable one, and proved the principle of targeting an oncogenic kinase. Impact on oncology drug development is paradigmatic.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery and project origin), Druker (clinical proof and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are reasonable. Contributions of Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, de Klein, Groffen and Baltimore for the underlying Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL biology are outside this credited set, and others at Ciba-Geigy (e.g. Zimmermann) are not listed.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of clinical data; fully mature and arguably late, with a risk that the discovery narrative is complicated by the chromosomal history.
uncertainties: Credit for chemistry (Zimmermann) and the Philadelphia chromosome lineage is not captured by the credited names.
Possibly seen as an extended-overdue recognition with a complex attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with population-level data showing large reductions in disease. A clear, major public health impact and a notable example of vaccine-based cancer prevention.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs; Frazer (with Zhou) contributed early VLP expression and the vaccine concept, and other groups (e.g. Kirnbauer, Rose/Georgetown) also have claims. A three-person configuration is plausible but contested at the margins.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation via trials and registry data showing reductions in cervical cancer; mature, though the zur Hausen prize (2008) already recognised the HPV-cancer link, which may affect committee appetite.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among VLP developers and the role of the late Jian Zhou are unresolved.
Prior recognition of HPV-cancer work may dilute urgency.
